analysis.investment_thesis: NEPHROPLUS trades at INR 586 against a Graham Number of approximately INR 116 — a 5x premium to intrinsic value — with losses in two of the last five years, utterly violating the foundational requirement of demonstrated earning power. No margin of safety exists; this is speculation dressed as investment.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.36 is below my 0.5 ceiling — balance sheet leverage is not alarming
Interest coverage of ~8x (Operating Income INR 167 Cr ÷ Finance Cost INR 21 Cr) is comfortably above my 3.5x floor
Operating cash flow positive all 5 years with FCF finally turning positive in 2025 (INR 35 Cr) — a nascent improvement
key_risks: P/E of 74.7 is nearly 5x my maximum of 15 — the price embeds years of rosy speculation, not proven facts
Net losses in FY2022 (-21 Cr) and FY2023 (-12 Cr) fail my 5-year consecutive positive earnings test outright
No dividend history — shareholders receive no cash return while management deploys capital in an unproven expansion into Uzbekistan, Philippines, and Saudi Arabia
red_flags: Graham Number ~INR 116 vs. market price INR 586 — stock trades at 5x intrinsic value by my calculation
Negative free cash flow for four consecutive years (2021–2024); only one year of positive FCF is not a track record
Capex accelerating (INR 101 Cr in FY2025) while cumulative retained earnings are thin — capital intensity is high relative to earning power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The arithmetic condemns this stock before any qualitative discussion begins. With EPS of approximately INR 7.46 and book value per share near INR 80, the Graham Number calculates to roughly INR 116. The market demands INR 586 — a five-fold premium. My method requires buying at a discount to intrinsic value, not at a fivefold markup. A P/E of 74.7 tells me that buyers are paying for a future that has not yet materialized and may never do so. The business produced losses as recently as FY2022 and FY2023; a company that cannot consistently earn money does not possess the "demonstrated earning power" I require as the foundation of any valuation.

The optimist will point to the revenue CAGR of 27.5% and the sharp improvement in operating income from INR 37 Cr (2021) to INR 167 Cr (2025). I acknowledge the trend is favorable. But Mr. Market has already capitalized every rupee of that improvement and then some. Dialysis is a structurally sound business — recurring, medically essential — yet the P/S of 5.52 and EV/EBITDA of 22.5 leave no room for error, competition, regulatory setbacks, or the simple passage of time. The intelligent investor does not pay for hope; he waits until the price offers compensation for the risk of being wrong. That price is not INR 586.
